activities.anchor: dashboards nobody opens, and slide decks that are technically accurate and completely uncompelling
activities.caption: three braided skills — file each move
activities.name: dashThreeSort

config.prompt: Seeing, monitoring or persuading? File each move:

items.label: identical summaries, four different worlds when plotted
the screen as a decision instrument, context on every tile
the encoding hierarchy ranked by decoding accuracy
start from the decision the screen supports

config.why: The failures follow: screens that go unopened, and stories that move no one.

activities.caption: pair each of the four with its plotted shape
activities.name: dashQuartetMatch

config.prompt: Pair each of the four with its plotted shape:

pairs.right: a perfect line spoiled by one outlier
a vertical column pinned at one x-value

config.why: Summaries compress; compression hides structure — outliers, curvature, clustering, data-entry errors.

activities.anchor: doubling a country's GDP and doubling its circle's
activities.caption: call the area distortion
activities.name: dashRadiusEst

config.prompt: The economy's size doubles and the circle's radius doubles with it — by what factor does the drawn area grow?
config.why: Radius is a square root of area: twice the radius, four times the area — proportionality violated.
config.context: One of the named sins, alongside dual axes, cherry-picked windows and cumulative curves.

activities.anchor: dashboard sprawl is a design failure
activities.caption: the screen estate — drag the divider
activities.name: dashSprawlCompare

config.prompt: The screen estate — drag the divider:

before.label: the sprawl
before.text: renamed metrics, silently broken pipelines, stale data manufacturing false confidence — an unowned metrics layer

after.label: the canonical layer
after.text: a small set of canonical, defined metrics with one home each — freshness owned, screens retired when the decision changes

config.why: A stale screen manufactures false confidence — ownership and staleness alerts belong to the maker, not IT housekeeping.

activities.anchor: a metric wobbling minute to minute is noise wearing urgency
activities.caption: bet before you read on — the professional-looking refresh rate
activities.name: dashFreshPredict

config.q: A weekly planning meeting is served by which screen?
choices: Weekly data — freshness matched to the decision, not the technology's capability
Real-time, updating every second — always more professional
Real-time, because visible jitter shows vigilance
Whatever cadence the pipeline happens to produce
config.why: Seconds-fresh pipelines cost real engineering and invite jitter into every glance — ask how stale the number may be before a wrong call gets made.

activities.anchor: Both invert the mystery-novel instinct that feels natural to analysts
activities.caption: the narrative spine, in order
activities.name: dashSCQAOrder

config.prompt: The frame that earns the answer — put it in order:
items: Complication — 'but the growth is concentrated in one segment, and it is slowing'
Question — 'where do we invest next quarter?'
Answer — 'here, with these three moves, at roughly this cost'
config.why: The frame turns charts into an argument; the pyramid turns an argument into a decision — rooms evaluate recommendations, not journeys.

activities.anchor: Uncertainty belongs in the story, told in plain words.
activities.caption: fill the blanks — the trust-building sentence
activities.name: dashUncertainCloze

config.text: 'Early signal: lift of %%0%% points, but the %%1%% still includes zero — we will have enough data in three weeks' builds trust; false precision ('up 1.14%!') %%2%% it. The compounding asset of an analyst's career is being the person whose %%3%% turned out to matter.
